title: Infosys Public Services CEO Lax Gopisetty Unreachable After Nepal Floods as Death Toll Hits 579
excerpt: The IT executive was visiting Nepal in a personal capacity when flash floods triggered by a glacier collapse killed hundreds and left nearly 2,000 missing, including 320 Indians
body:
• Infosys Public Services CEO Lax Gopisetty, who was visiting Nepal in a personal capacity, is currently unreachable following devastating floods that struck the Himalayan nation on August 26.
  • Nepal's death toll has risen to 579, with 1,924 people still missing — including 517 foreign nationals and 98 Indians — as rescue operations continue across flood-ravaged districts.
  • India's Ministry of External Affairs confirmed 320 Indian nationals remain missing or uncontactable, while 149 Indians have crossed safely from China into Nepal and roughly 400 are safe inside China.
  • A dammed lake formed by the mudslide on the Tibetan side of the border is at risk of breaching, prompting Nepalese authorities to order evacuations and threatening a second wave of flooding.

Infosys confirmed on Friday that Lax Gopisetty, chief executive officer of its US and Canada-focused subsidiary Infosys Public Services, is unreachable after the catastrophic floods that tore through Nepal's northern Rasuwa district two days ago.

"We can confirm that our colleague Lax Gopisetty, who was visiting the region in a personal capacity, is currently not reachable," the Bengaluru-headquartered IT services giant said in a statement. "We remain in close communication with the family and are providing all necessary support during this difficult time."

Death Toll Climbs to 579

Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority raised the confirmed death toll to 579 on Friday evening, an increase of 41 within hours. The number of missing people has surged to 1,924, including 933 from hydroelectric power projects, 517 foreign nationals, and 127 Nepali citizens living abroad who were visiting the country.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=wfQF7IKT01g

Among the missing foreign tourists, 98 are Indian nationals and 65 are Americans, according to the Nepal Tourism Board. Chitwan recorded the highest body count at 233, followed by Nawalparasi East at 154, Gorkha at 46, and Dhading at 40.

Nearly 800 people have been rescued so far, while 101 injured individuals are receiving hospital treatment. Nepal has deployed more than 15,000 security personnel for search and rescue operations.

320 Indians Still Uncontactable

India's Ministry of External Affairs said on Friday that 320 Indian nationals remain missing or uncontactable in the aftermath of the disaster. The ministry confirmed that 149 Indians crossed safely from China into Nepal and released a full list of evacuees. Approximately 400 Indian nationals are currently safe inside China, with the Indian Embassy in active contact to facilitate their evacuation.

"Our thoughts are with Lax and all those affected by this tragedy."

— Infosys statement

Glacier Collapse Triggered the Disaster

The U.S. Geological Survey determined that the catastrophe was triggered by a massive glacier collapse rather than an earthquake as initially suspected. Experts believe a vast quantity of rock and ice fell from around 16,000 feet, plunging 4,000 feet into the valley below and generating a devastating flood wave that barreled through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers.

The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development in Kathmandu noted that water levels on the Trishuli River rose by as much as 27 feet in just 30 minutes. The floodwaters carried debris and victims as far as 150 miles downstream to districts near Nepal's southern border with India.

Second Flood Wave Feared

Nepalese authorities on Friday urgently ordered evacuations in affected areas after early signs of a breach appeared in a dammed lake formed by the mudslide on the Tibetan side of the border. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that the lake, holding an estimated 2.5 million cubic meters of water, has begun overflowing, forcing a temporary suspension of rescue operations.

The Red Cross estimates that nearly 93,000 people have been affected by the disaster and expects the death toll to rise. India has offered all possible assistance to Nepal as the search for survivors continues.
